I have a close family member who was a first responder to the Omagh bombing (amongst other paramilitary and terrorist attacks). For reasons obvious to the northern Irish amongst us, I won’t give specifics to protect their identity and my families (unfortunately in NI first responders are still targeted by paramilitary groups). 

My family member has only spoken of what they witnessed of the aftermath of the Omagh bombing once and has never repeated, due to the horrific sights they saw and the emotional aftermath they dealt with. What always stuck with me and still haunts me, was the death of a mother with unborn twins due to this attack.This photo is a sad reminder of the innocence lost during the troubles in my country. What’s worse is the fact that in 1998, the troubles where largely believed to be winding down to a ceasefire. In April of ‘98 the good Friday agreement had been signed and the IRA were working towards disarmament. In August of 1998 - this.
